claims.text: The local Japanese pre-English catalog models the First Official Pokemon Card Game Tournament trophy source slice with a June 14-15, 1997 event window.
The source slice models three source-pinned trophy card identities: No.1 Trainer 011, No.2 Trainer 012, and No.3 Trainer 013.

Selected source lines describe the 1st Official Pokemon Card Game Tournament as held June 14-15, 1997, with four tournament sessions and No.1/No.2/No.3 Trainer cards awarded to the corresponding place winners across those sessions.
Selected source lines report four copies of each No.1, No.2, and No.3 Trainer card were given out; this tranche records that as selected-source context, not official surviving-copy authority.
Selected source lines explicitly warn that the 1st official tournament No.1-3 Trainer cards and trophies are often confused with Charizard/Lizardon Mega Battle No.1-3 Trainer cards.
This source slice matters because it captures Pokemon TCG organized play becoming material: rank, session, trophy, and card identity fused into a tiny event ledger.
The local rows credit all three trophy cards to Mitsuhiro Arita, scoped as provider metadata and not direct physical-card print proof.

Local catalog examples connect Mitsuhiro Arita to many early card memories; this tranche uses that only as local artist-footprint context and not as a complete biography or same-art equivalence claim.

Agents should preserve First Official Tournament context, June 14-15, 1997 event window, rank number, source row 011-013, Arita credit, selected-source copy-count caveat, and Charizard/Lizardon Mega Battle confusion boundary before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: First Official Tournament trophies — when rank became cardboard
narrative.why_it_matters: This is where competitive Pokemon stops being only play and becomes ceremony. Four sessions, three ranks, three Arita trophy cards: the event made a scoreboard you could hold. The beauty is also the danger for agents: trophy language is magnetic, so rank, event, row, and the not-Charizard-Mega-Battle boundary have to stay bolted on.

Selected source lines identify No.1 Trainer as the 1st place trophy card awarded across each of four tournament sessions at the June 14-15, 1997 event.

No.1 Trainer is the sharpest edge of the first official tournament story: not just a trophy card, but a card that says competitive Pokemon had learned to make victory into an object.
No.1 Trainer is part of a rank trio; its identity depends on the first-place rank, the 1997 First Official Tournament context, and source row 011, not name alone.
